correctness.rationale: The exact metric with m>=2, 0<s<=2 admits D_p=B_p tensor J_m+s^p I_5 tensor (J_m-I_m). Its centered zero-sum spectrum has eigenvalues -s^p (multiplicity 5(m-1)), E1=m(a-b*2^p)+(m-1)s^p<=-1 (multiplicity 2) and E2=m(-b+a*2^p)+(m-1)s^p (multiplicity 2). E2(0)=-1, E2 is strictly convex, and E2 tends to infinity, so there is exactly one positive crossing. The equation m*a*2^p+(m-1)*s^p=m*b and the two-dimensional critical nullspace follow. Setting h_s(p)=a(2^p-1)+(s^p-1) gives at s_c=2^-a the vanishing first derivative and second derivative (log 2)^2, yielding the three m-asymptotic orders (constant, m^-1/2, m^-1), with the stated constants. The p=1 boundary follows by substituting E2(1)<=0. Independently constructed full matrices at four (m,s) values, diagonalized their zero-sum restrictions at analytic endpoints, and found eigenvalue errors <=7.9e-13. Numerical tests corroborate but do not prove all sizes/parameters.

value.rationale: Supremal negative type measures optimal Hilbert snowflake exponent of a natural five-cluster cycle metric. Determining every m,s endpoint, critical embedding rank, and sharp transition between nonvanishing, 1/sqrt(m), and 1/m scaling gives a motivated infinite-family classification; it is not merely the known ordinary five-cycle calculation.

limitations: Exactly five equal-size clusters, 0<s<=2; does not classify unequal clusters, other base graphs or arbitrary metrics.
The spectrum proof establishes all m and s; finite matrix tests alone do not.
